players.product: filtration, ultra-pure materials handling & deposition materials

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results: CFO Linda LaGorga said Q4 sales were $824 million, at the high end of guidance, down 3% year over year and up 2% sequentially. CEO David Reeder said revenue, gross margin, adjusted EBITDA margin and non-GAAP EPS were all at the high end of or above guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was 27.7% of revenue, non-GAAP EPS was $0.70 per share (above guidance) and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.32. Higher production volumes across the factories drove the sequential gross margin increase. The CEO said gross margin rose to 44% in Q4 from 43.6 in Q3, after he had guided a trough of 43-44%. Full-year 2025 revenue was approximately flat with 2024, excluding divestitures.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales $824 million (down 3% YoY, up 2% sequentially); adjusted EBITDA 27.7% of revenue; non-GAAP EPS $0.70; gross margin 44%

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 segments: Materials Solutions sales were $362 million, flat year over year and up 4% sequentially. Advanced deposition materials drove most of the sequential growth, helped by demand for moly deposition in NAND. The segment's adjusted operating margin was 20.9%. Advanced Purity Solutions sales were $465 million, down 5% year over year and up 1% sequentially. Fluid Handling and FOUPs drove the year-over-year decline, partly offset by strong growth in liquid filtration, which had another record quarter. The APS adjusted operating margin was 24.8%. The CFO said the year-over-year margin decline came from costs related to ramping the Taiwan and Colorado manufacturing sites and lower production volumes, and the sequential decrease from unfavorable product mix and the timing of operating expenses.
quarterly_data.figure: Materials Solutions $362 million (flat YoY, up 4% sequentially), adjusted operating margin 20.9%; Advanced Purity Solutions $465 million (down 5% YoY, up 1% sequentially), adjusted operating margin 24.8%

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 revenue drivers: unit-driven revenue grew approximately 2% in 2025, in line with wafer starts, led by CMP consumables, liquid filtration and selective etch. CapEx-driven revenue declined 7%, matching the drop in industry fab construction CapEx, which the CEO described as 'down high single digits, call it seven ish percent'. The drop was most visible in the FOUP and Fluid Handling product lines in the APS division. About 75% of revenue is unit-driven and tracks MSI (wafer starts); the other 25% is tied to industry CapEx. Roughly two-thirds of that CapEx-related revenue follows fab construction spending and one-third follows WFE. Early in 2026, management said order patterns for these CapEx-linked product lines were already starting to recover.
quarterly_data.figure: unit-driven revenue grew approximately 2%; CapEx-driven revenue declined 7% (2025); about 75% of revenue unit-driven / 25% tied to industry CapEx

quarterly_data.signal: End-market mix: more than 60% of Entegris' revenue comes from advanced logic (seven nanometers and below) and advanced memory (the two newest memory generations). AI is not the majority of these advanced nodes, but management called it the most significant growth driver and expects the advanced share to keep rising. About 40% of revenue comes from advanced logic, about 30% from mainstream logic and the rest from memory. Memory is about 30% of total revenue, split roughly half NAND and half DRAM.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 60% of revenue from advanced logic + advanced memory; about 40% advanced logic, about 30% mainstream logic, memory about 30% (about half NAND, half DRAM)

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 logic and industry outlook: management expects Entegris to benefit from node transitions in both logic and memory. Rising demand for two-nanometer devices should meaningfully lift wafer output through 2026, and that node carries both higher content per wafer and strong share for Entegris. Advanced logic fab utilization is already near 100%, and customers are investing aggressively in more capacity. At the most advanced logic node, Entegris has secured strong POR (position of record) positions in CMP consumables, advanced deposition and implant materials, liquid purification and filtration, and wafer handling. The team is now focused on winning incremental share and PORs at subsequent advanced nodes. Separately, the CEO said it takes time to grow two-nanometer and to transition to new nodes such as 1.4 nanometer. Management expects 'middish single-digit' industry MSI (wafer starts) growth in 2026 and strong WFE growth. Fab construction CapEx should grow modestly after last year's high single-digit decline, weighted to the second half, with a bigger acceleration in 2027 as work starts on new fabs. Management flagged ongoing memory shortages as a possible second-half 2026 risk for mainstream end markets; guidance assumes no impact.
quarterly_data.figure: middish single-digit industry MSI growth expected in 2026; advanced logic utilization near 100%

quarterly_data.signal: NAND: the move from roughly 250 layers to approximately 300 layers is under way. Management expects more than 20% NAND bit growth in 2026, driven mainly by higher-layer, higher-capacity NAND rather than a big increase in wafer starts. Entegris expects a double-digit increase in its NAND content per wafer as customers move to higher layer counts and adopt new materials such as moly and selective etch. It has won strong POR positions in NAND deposition materials, CMP and selective etch. NAND utilization is around 85%, and layer-count increases are absorbing most of the remaining 15% of capacity, with fewer new wafer starts. If demand stays strong, flash makers will likely need to add significant fab capacity, setting up higher NAND MSI growth in 2027. The CEO said Entegris gains from both layer growth and wafer growth, with slightly more from a full wafer start.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 20% NAND bit growth expected in 2026; double-digit increase in NAND content per wafer; NAND utilization around 85%

quarterly_data.signal: DRAM, HBM and advanced packaging: DRAM capacity was nearly fully utilized at the end of 2025, and management expects it to stay that way through 2026. More DRAM is shifting from standalone DDR5 into HBM, which adds some content per wafer, though less than a new wafer start would. Management expects tight supply in HBM, DDR5 and advanced packaging to require additional fab capacity heading into 2027. Entegris is gaining traction in DRAM and HBM, particularly with CMP consumables and advanced packaging solutions. The CEO said advanced packaging revenue grew nicely in 2025, to 'roughly a $100 million plus minus', and should keep growing in 2026. Several product lines for advanced packaging are sampling now and more will sample later in the year, so the larger benefit is expected in 2027 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging revenue roughly $100 million (2025), expected to keep growing in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex: the multiyear manufacturing capex cycle that began in 2022 is complete. Capex was $299 million in 2025 (approximately 9% of sales) and is expected to fall to $250 million in 2026, returning longer term to approximately 7% to 8% of sales. Management said the new capacity plus the existing base can deliver significantly more than $1 billion in incremental revenue with limited further investment. The Taiwan facility is still ramping, and the Colorado facility should substantially complete key customer product qualifications in 2026. Entegris exited its Chester, Pennsylvania facility in Q4 and expects to rationalize at least one additional facility in 2026. Free cash flow was $404 million in 2025, a 12.7% margin (up nearly 300 basis points year over year). Net leverage ended 2025 at 3.8 times, against a target of below 3.5 times by the end of 2026, and Entegris paid down $300 million of its term loan during 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $299 million; 2026 capex expected $250 million; capacity supports significantly more than $1 billion incremental revenue; 2025 free cash flow $404 million (12.7% margin)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance: sales of $785 million to $825 million, up approximately 4% year over year at the midpoint (slightly more than 6% at the high end, per the CEO). GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin of 44.5 to 45.5%, including about 100 basis points of benefit from a change in asset useful lives (about 44% on a normalized basis). EBITDA margin of 26.5% to 27.5% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.70 to $0.78. Q2 2026 sales are expected to rise 1% to 3% from Q1, in line with normal seasonality, and the CEO said order patterns support that range. FY2026 modeling items: capex $250 million, depreciation $150 million, net interest expense approximately $190 million. Management will keep guiding one quarter at a time and called the timing of fab CapEx through the year the wild card.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 sales $785 million to $825 million (approximately 4% YoY at midpoint); gross margin 44.5 to 45.5%; non-GAAP EPS $0.70 to $0.78; Q2 sales up 1% to 3% sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: China and local-for-local supply: the CFO said China was 21% of revenue in both 2024 and 2025, with dollars down slightly. The CEO said the biggest obstacle in China is guaranteeing supply, so in 2025 Entegris qualified more manufacturing in Asia. About 85% of Q1 2026 China revenue will be supplied from Asia facilities, rising to around or above 90% during 2026. Expected China growth drivers in 2026 are some CapEx-related product lines, liquid filtration and CMP products. Separately, discussing mainstream markets (not China), the CEO said silicon carbide, where Entegris sells a CMP solution, was a headwind in 2025 but is now stable and may improve slowly in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: China 21% of revenue (2024 and 2025); about 85% of Q1 2026 China revenue supplied from Asia facilities; heading to around or greater than 90% in 2026
